sentences.ko: 이걸 다 어떻게 나한테 숨길 수가 있어?
sentences.text: How could you have kept all of this from me?

alts.text: You kept all this from me? Seriously?
I cannot believe that you concealed all of this from me.

sentences.note: **kept all of this from me** 는 '나한테 이걸 다 숨겼다'는 뜻이에요. 믿었던 사람이 중요한 일을 말 안 해 줬다는 걸 알았을 때 서운함을 터뜨리며 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 저녁 하라고 시켜 놓고는 한 시간이나 늦게 오고, 내가 딱 하나 부탁한 것까지 까먹었잖아.
sentences.text: You forced me to make dinner, then you're an hour late and you forget the one little thing that I asked you to do.

alts.text: So I cook, you show up an hour late, and you forgot the one thing I asked for?
I made dinner because you insisted, yet you arrived an hour late and did not remember the single small thing I requested.

sentences.note: **the one little thing** 는 '딱 하나, 그것도 별것 아닌 부탁'을 강조해서 상대를 탓할 때 써요. **an hour late** 처럼 늦은 시간을 앞에 붙이면 '한 시간이나 늦었다'는 말이 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.text: His flight doesn't leave for another 45 more minutes.

alts.text: He's got 45 minutes till his flight.
There are still forty-five minutes before his flight departs.

sentences.note: **doesn't leave for another** 45 minutes 는 '45분은 더 있어야 떠난다', 즉 아직 시간 있다고 다독일 때 쓰는 말이에요. another 와 more 를 둘 다 쓴 건 말하다 보면 나오는 겹침이라, 따라 할 때는 한쪽만 써도 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 결혼할 때 내 연락처 수첩을 너희한테 물려줬어야 했는데.
sentences.text: I should have given you guys my black book when I got married.

alts.text: Man, I should've handed you guys my black book after the wedding.
It would have been wise to pass my black book on to you when I married.

sentences.note: **black book** 은 예전에 만나던 이성들 연락처를 모아 둔 수첩을 농담처럼 부르는 말이에요. **should have given** 은 '줬어야 했는데' 하고 지나간 일을 아쉬워할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 벌써 애들 이름까지 다 정해 놨구나.
sentences.text: You already know what your kids' names are going to be.

alts.text: Wow, you've got the kids' names all picked out?
It seems you have already decided what your children will be named.

sentences.note: **what your kids' names are going to be** 는 아직 생기지도 않은 아이들 이름을 미리 정해 둔 사람에게 놀라거나 놀리듯 할 때 써요. 캐주얼하게는 **all picked out** 으로 '다 골라 놨다'고 합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.ko: 너 담배 피우는 거 이제 진짜 지긋지긋해. 그래서 끊는 데 도움 될 만한 거 하나 가져왔어.
sentences.text: Well, I'm really sick of your smoking, so I brought something that is going to help you quit.

alts.text: Ugh, your smoking's driving me nuts, so I got you something to help you quit.
I have grown very tired of your smoking, so I have brought something that will help you stop.

sentences.note: **sick of** 는 '~가 지긋지긋하다'로, 참을 만큼 참았을 때 씁니다. 담배나 술을 '끊다'는 **quit** 하나면 되고, '끊게 도와주다'는 **help you quit** 이라고 합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그럼 차라리 내가 남겠다고 하는 게 낫겠다.
sentences.text: Well, then I might as well offer to stay.

alts.text: Guess I'll just offer to stay, then.
In that case, it would make sense for me to offer to remain.

sentences.note: **might as well** 은 '어차피 이렇게 된 거 차라리 ~하는 게 낫겠다'는 뜻입니다. 다른 방법이 마땅치 않아서 그쪽을 고를 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그냥 친구로 지내면 왜 안 되는데?
sentences.text: Why can't Why can't we just hang out as friends?

alts.text: Can't we just hang out, like, as friends?
Is there any reason we cannot simply spend time together as friends?

sentences.note: **hang out** 은 특별한 계획 없이 같이 어울려 노는 것을 말합니다. **as friends** 를 붙이면 '사귀는 사이 말고 친구로'라는 뜻이 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 나 대학 때문에 이 도시로 올라온 거야.
sentences.text: I uh came to the city for college.

alts.text: Moved here for college, actually.
I originally moved to this city to attend university.

sentences.note: '대학 다니려고'를 길게 풀 필요 없이 **for college** 라고만 하면 됩니다. 미국에서는 대학을 보통 university 보다 **college** 라고 말합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아, 오늘 밤엔 누구랑 뽀뽀할 기분이 아니야.
sentences.text: Oh, I don't feel like kissing anyone tonight.

alts.text: Nah, not in the mood to kiss anybody tonight.
I would rather not kiss anyone this evening.

sentences.note: **don't feel like** 뒤에 -ing 를 붙이면 '~할 기분이 아니다'라는 말이 됩니다. 같은 뜻으로 **not in the mood** 도 자주 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends
